citation.title: Composite 3D-printed Plate-based Mechanical Metamaterials
citation.authors: Aya Hosoi, Jier Wang, Yuki Fujita, Tatsuo Tanaka, Junichi Takahashi, Ajit Panesar
citation.venue: 24th International Conference on Composite Materials (ICCM-24), Baltimore, 4-8 August 2025, session 'Design, Repair and Lifecycle'; conference paper deposited in the ICCM-24 Zenodo community (record 18597654, CC BY-SA 4.0)
citation.version_coded: Conference paper PDF ICCM24_Final_Paper_054.pdf (9 pages) from Zenodo record 18597654, the record the pool's concept DOI resolves to; read in full

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Not coded (excluded). Headline: low-resolution SIMP, per-element stiffness-tensor optimization and an MLP inverse generator give graded lattices whose simulated three-point-bending specific stiffness beats uniform lattices (165.1 vs 162.5 Nylon; 335.6 vs 229.4 Onyx).
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Not coded (excluded at full text). No runtime of any method is reported.

notes: Excluded under PROTOCOL §4 and the 2026-09-24 FT-NOBASELINE clarification. The only comparisons are graded (optimal) lattices vs uniform lattices of the same cell type (Table 4, FEA of a three-point-bending test in Abaqus) and truss-based vs plate-based BCC cells from the same pipeline (Table 5: 143.9 vs 671.4). No classical optimizer (inverse homogenization, dehomogenization or full-scale TO) is run, timed or cited for its cost or result; these appear only as background (Sec. 1). The low-resolution SIMP step is part of the proposed pipeline, not a comparator. Earlier codes checked: FT-SCOPE does not apply (multiscale TO with ML-based lattice inverse generation is in scope); FT-TYPE does not apply (a full conference paper, eligible under §3.3); FT-FORWARD does not apply (the MLP maps a target stiffness tensor and volume fraction to cell parameters, an inverse design step); FT-MLONLY does not apply (no ML comparator either). Method details: MLP inverse generator trained on 5,000 random unit cells with numerically homogenized stiffness tensors (Sec. 2.1.2); volume fraction 0.5; penalty 2.6 (2D) and 3 (3D) (Sec. 2.1). The authors note that the optimization boundary conditions (half MBB beam, fixed) differ from the validation (three-point bending with contact), and orthotropy was not modelled in the FEA validation (Secs. 2.2 and 3.1). Related but distinct: P00589 (Wang and Panesar 2022, the 2D method this paper extends). Access: Zenodo record via its public API and file link, generic User-Agent, no personal data. Author 'Jier Wang' is not Jun Wang; no author named Jun Wang. Screening code was I-UNCLEAR.
